title: The Healing Hands
text: Two stone hands rise from the shrine's floor, cupped as if to hold water, worn smooth and dark by a thousand years of pilgrims. Old blood stains the palms. Pilgrims lay their wounds in them, and some of them walk away whole, and some of them leave something behind.

options.label: The most wounded lays their wound in the stone hands, praying they are among the lucky.

outcomes.text: The hands close, warm as flesh, and open again, and the wound is gone. Something in the stone keeps the memory of it.

options.label: All of you lay a hand there, and share whatever the stone gives.

outcomes.text: A warmth that spreads up the arm and lasts.

options.label: Pry out the jewels in the palms. The pilgrims have had their use of them.

outcomes.text: The stone hands close on the thief's fingers, slowly, and grind, and only let go when they are paid.
